article.title: RECAP: 2026 Member Mobilization Institute
article.author: Joe Simpson
article.content: RECAP: 2026 Member Mobilization Institute ONAWAY, MI – UAW members from across the country gathered at Black Lake for the 2026 Member Mobilization Institute, a week of learning new skills, sharing ideas, and exploring how we can strengthen our union together. Workshops, discussions, and hands-on practice challenged participants to consider what it takes to build lasting power and to prepare for the opportunities and challenges ahead, including May Day 2028. Learning continued beyond the classroom as delegates embraced opportunities to share their own worker stories by creating art with block printing, bandanas, signs, buttons, photography, and zines. Creativity became a powerful organizing tool, helping participants communicate their message, connect with others, and find their entry point in the movement. From inspiring art exhibits to a memorable evening that blended live music and labor history, delegates experienced firsthand how culture helps strengthen our collective action. Participants from across our nine regions, including Puerto Rico, formed new friendships and strengthened old connections, whether testing their knowledge at trivia, singing karaoke together, or joining a nature trail walk. As they return home, delegates carry fresh skills, new connections, and a renewed commitment to building active, engaged locals. The work ahead belongs to all of us, and this year’s Institute was a reminder that the strength of our union lives in the solidarity of its members and in what we’re determined to build together.
